results.title: Understanding Your FEMA Letter | FEMA.gov
results.content:
### Approved

If you are approved for FEMA assistance, your letter will explain how much money you will get and what the money can be used for.

Please read your entire letter as it will explain how to ask for more help if you need it.

### Next Steps if You’re Not Approved

If you are not approved for FEMA assistance, your letter will explain what to do if you disagree with FEMA’s decision. You can send more information to show why you need help, like repair estimates or an insurance settlement, and we will take another look at your case.

Look for the section labeled “Your Next Steps” to find out which documents FEMA needs from you.

## Appeal Form [...] ## Appeal Form

At the end of your letter, look for an appeal form that can be used to send us additional information about your situation. You may also download the appeal form.

This form can help make sure you have the information FEMA needs and gives you a space to explain any important context why you need help. If it's easier to just write us a letter, that's fine too. Sending an appeal form or letter with your additional information is optional.

For more information on how to file an appeal, visit How Do I Appeal FEMA's Decision?

Note: You still may be eligible for FEMA assistance even if your insurance doesn't cover all of your losses or expenses. Just keep in mind that FEMA cannot give you money for what your insurance already paid for.

## If FEMA Needs More Information from You

FEMA wants to help as much as we can. Sometimes we need some additional information like an insurance settlement, copy of a receipt for disaster costs, or documents that confirm your identity and where you live.

Learn more about what to expect

### Review FEMA’s Decision

Once FEMA has reviewed your application, the results of the inspection and/or documentation submitted, you will get a letter explaining:

 whether you are approved for assistance
 how much assistance you will receive
 how the assistance must be used
 how to appeal FEMA’s decision if you do not agree with it

The letter will be sent to you by email or mail based on what you selected when you completed your application.

### Frequently Asked Questions and Rumors [...] alert - warning

The last day for individuals and families to apply for assistance after this disaster has passed.

To check the status of your application, visit DisasterAssistance.gov.

### I Applied for Assistance. What's Next?

After applying for assistance, your request is reviewed to determine if an inspection is needed to verify disaster-related damage to your home and personal property. FEMA staff and inspectors may contact you to discuss your disaster-caused damage.

FEMA may also request more information to support your eligibility for assistance or information related to your specific disaster-related needs identified in your application. If this is needed, you will receive a letter from FEMA outlining the information needed.
